data.narrative:
Hadrian, a Series C robotics and manufacturing company founded by Chris Power, is currently valued at $1.6B post-money on $1.37B total raised. The valuation exercise references a peer universe of nine companies: one public (277810.KQ) and eight private-stage robotics firms including Exotec, Agile Robots, Bedrock Robotics, Dexterity, and Nimble Robotics, spanning Series B through Series D.

Two triangulation methods apply here. Stage-progression analysis, applying a 1.7x multiplier typical of Series C-to-next-stage progression against the $1.6B base, yields $2.7B. Peer-median analysis across six same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables produces a $1.7B implied value; the peer set ranges from $1.0B (Agile Robots, Series C) to $2.0B (Exotec Series D, Generalist AI Series B), with a median of $1.7B.

The two methods triangulate to a range of $1.4B to $3.1B, with a median of $2.2B. The current $1.6B valuation sits at the low end, suggesting modest upside to median expectations. Key uncertainties include stage-specific milestone achievement (Series C companies show wide dispersion in the peer set), and the limited public comparability data. The gap between the stage-progression result ($2.7B) and peer-median ($1.7B) reflects heterogeneity in robotics subsector maturity and growth profiles.
